sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Iranian military spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, via Ynet, Sat Nov 7] 'The armed forces of the Islamic Republic are now on higher alert and more powerful than they were at the beginning of the war. On the orders of the supreme leader, any response by the armed forces will be immediate, effective and without geographical limits.' [VERIFIED CONTEXT] The warning follows Friday's limited US strikes on Qeshm Island air defences (recorded 0700-01) and comes as Trump weighs a decision on resuming major operations (1100-01). Iran has previously threatened to expand retaliation beyond the Middle East if attacked (WSJ Nov 7).
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct declared-tier family (Ynetnews T3) relaying the actor's own statement. No second family carried the Akraminia statement in-window. The statement IS the primary source (Iran's military speaking for itself), so the single-family record is explicit per the pass-gate rule; the claim keeps its PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM label and is NOT presented as independently verified fact about Iranian capability.
sections.what_disputed: The 'stronger than at the beginning of the war' claim is Tehran's own assertion and is contradicted by the reported scale of damage to Iran's air defences (US officials: most systems destroyed or severely degraded in June 2025 + current conflict; WSJ Nov 7). No independent evidence of the claimed strength was offered. The warning is a statement of intent, not a verified capability.
sections.why_matters: Iran's military warns its next response will have 'no geographical limits' -- on the supreme leader's orders. Pair the threat with the counterpoint: US officials say Iran's air defences are already largely destroyed. Warning vs capability is the story.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Ynet, Saturday Nov 7; zero 'Akraminia'/'geographical limit' mentions in any prior Nov 6/7 scan -- grep confirms) -- Iran's military spokesman Mohammad Akraminia warns Saturday that Iran's armed forces are stronger than at the war's start and any response will be 'immediate, effective and without geographical limits', on the supreme leader's orders

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran's military warns its next response will have 'no geographical limits' -- on the supreme leader's orders. Pair the threat with the counterpoint: US officials say Iran's air defences are already largely destroyed. Warning vs capability is the story. The fault line our audience is arguing over: 'Without geographical limits' -- is Iran's warning a real threat to expand the war beyond the Middle East, or a bluff from a military whose air defences are already shattered?
